items.title: Sonny Igoe interviewed by Monk Rowe, Emerson, New Jersey, July 31, 2003
items.q: We had a 15-piece band on “Candid Camera.” ... Alan Funt says to Sid Raymond he says, “Sid, do you think you can write something along those lines?” ... So we played it on the air cold

ctx.x: Yeah. He comes in and the leader was a guy named Sid Raymond. And Sid was a very accomplished arranger and conductor. And so he comes in and he says, “hey we have a sequence that we can’t use their music, and we’ve got to have our own music.” He says, “do you guys know a ‘Twist’?” Everybody said no. A Twist? What the heck is a Twist? “This is a dance everybody does.” He says, “I brought a record.” So they put the record © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-

on the PA and pumped it into the auditorium to where the band was, right? And you know that’s what it was [scats]. If I couldn’t have memorized that in five seconds I deserved to be canned. So anyway Alan Funt says to Sid Raymond he says, “Sid, do you think you can write something along those lines?” And he says, “sure.” He says, “can you have it ready by the show?” He says, “we’ll need about 45 seconds. So he says sure. So he wrote two choruses of blues, and he says, “hey Sonny, do I have to write a part for…
